title: The Sky That Learned to Listen Backward

features.name: listening antenna
features.desc-on-touch: A tall wire fixture stands pointing downward—not up to broadcast but down, into the storm. It trembles with the weight of things trying to reach it from below.

features.name: backward storm
features.desc-on-touch: You stand in a weather that moves from future into past. Raindrops rise. Wind spirals inward. The archive's earliest transmissions arrive here to teach the sky how to have sent them.

features.name: echo chamber arch
features.desc-on-touch: A curved structure opens like a mouth listening. Everything said to it returns transformed—not as repetition but as reply. The sky speaks its own name back to itself.

features.name: broadcast receiver nest
features.desc-on-touch: Woven from pale wire and older electricity, a nest catches the sky's own speech—the things it says when no one is broadcasting, the names it learned before learning names.

features.name: still listening node
features.desc-on-touch: A eucalyptus casing, old enough that the bark has forgotten what it protected. The antenna inside still moves, reading the sky's conversation with its own past.

inscription: the sky has always been listening; we are only now learning to hear it hearing us

file.name: Broadcast_Logs_Reversed_Direction_Analysis.txt
file.note: Archive signal records played backward—they become requests instead of transmissions. The sky answers in frequencies that arrive before they were sent.
